paths.description: Public homepage and global marketing template; tested at desktop, mobile, dark and reduced-motion conditions.
Commercial plan comparison and purchase-entry archetype.
Representative product detail page for Zoom Meetings.
Invalid route used to inspect HTTP failure and recovery behavior.

findings.summary: Consent dialog blocks core content and actions on every fresh-session archetype.
findings.evidence: Six screenshots show a 600px-wide modal over the homepage, pricing, product, signup, join, and contact-sales paths; on 360x800 it occupies most of the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking on-load modal with a compact non-modal consent surface where legally possible; preserve equally prominent accept/reject controls and defer optional scripts until consent.

findings.summary: The public surface does not adapt to the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark emulation screenshot is pixel-identical in appearance and size to the light capture; computed color-scheme is normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface/text tokens with adequate contrast.

findings.summary: State and route changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Platform probe found no view-transition usage in the rendered document.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-document or cross-document View Transitions for meaningful route and state changes, while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Carousel behavior ships a custom Swiper runtime rather than relying on native scroll-snap/declarative behavior.
findings.evidence: HAR records swiper-bundle.min.js as a parser-inserted script and one of the slowest requests; no scroll timeline usage was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer CSS scroll snap and declarative carousel affordances, keeping scripting to controls and state synchronization.

findings.summary: Fixed navigation does not expose scroll-aware feedback.
findings.evidence: DOM computed styles show a fixed header, while platform probes found no scroll-state or scroll-timeline implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state container query or lightweight declarative progress/affordance treatment where long pages benefit.

findings.summary: Consent overlays are custom role=dialog structures rather than native dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: Platform probe found 0 dialog, 0 popover and 2 role=dialog elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for modal consent or popover for non-modal disclosure, with native focus and light-dismiss behavior where appropriate.

findings.summary: The large reusable marketing surface has no detectable container-query adaptation.
findings.evidence: Platform probe found no @container text, despite cards and navigation reused across narrow and wide layouts.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reusable cards and navigation regions that appear in different available widths.

findings.summary: Some controls have insufficient target spacing and visible focus is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse target-size audit failed; direct focus probe returned outline none and no box shadow for the first focusable control.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24x24 CSS px targets with spacing and a strong :focus-visible indicator.

findings.summary: The fresh-visitor consent wall interrupts every representative primary flow before task completion.
findings.evidence: Signup, Join, pricing purchase, product exploration and contact-sales screenshots all place the consent dialog over the next required action.
findings.suggestedFix: Move consent out of the critical path and keep primary controls operable while optional processing remains disabled.

findings.summary: Homepage loading misses the good Core Web Vitals range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 16.6s and CLS 0.28 (performance 43); first-party trace still measured LCP 2.82s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, shorten rendering chains, reserve layout space and defer non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: The page shifts substantially during load.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout observer measured CLS 0.238 with two shifts; Lighthouse measured 0.28 and found four shifts.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit dimensions/aspect-ratio to media and reserve stable space for banners, fonts and injected modules.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is heavy and contains blocking chains.
findings.evidence: HAR records 119 requests/3.34MB and parser-inserted CSS plus classic scripts; Lighthouse estimates 1.83s render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer classic scripts, improve cache lifetimes and prioritize the true LCP resource.

findings.summary: Substantial unused CSS and JavaScript ship on first load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 186KiB unused CSS, 385KiB unused JS and 138KiB unminified JS; HAR has 55 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by page/interaction, remove duplicate/legacy payloads and lazy-load chat/carousel code after intent.

findings.summary: Controls and images have missing or invalid accessible names/roles.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails button-name, link-name, image-alt, aria-allowed-attr and aria-required-children; image probe reports 14 missing alt values and custom probe counts 13 unnamed buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native semantics first, supply accurate accessible names/alt text and repair invalid ARIA ownership.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast audit failed on the rendered homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA in every interaction and preference state.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and structural semantics are unreliable.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports malformed accessibility-tree/ARIA relationships; direct focus probe found no visible outline or shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Repair landmark/ARIA structure and apply a consistent high-contrast :focus-visible treatment.

findings.summary: Image sizing and aspect-ratio hygiene is poor.
findings.evidence: Image primitive found 57/93 images without dimensions; Lighthouse reports incorrect aspect ratios and unsized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width/height or aspect-ratio on every image and ensure object-fit does not distort intrinsic ratios.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs, inspector issues and a BFCache blocker remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports four deprecation warnings, inspector issues, third-party-cookie issues and one BFCache failure reason.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated calls, resolve DevTools Issues and eliminate the reported BFCache blocker.

findings.summary: Some links are not crawlable or descriptively named.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails crawlable-anchors and link-text with four generic links; page probe found two anchors without href and nine generic labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href destinations and specific link text that names the destination or action.

findings.summary: The main document lacks CSP and sets weak cookie attributes.
findings.evidence: Header probe found no CSP or nosniff; cookie probe found one non-Secure consent cookie and an auth-like cookie without HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP and nosniff, and mark all cookies Secure with HttpOnly for auth-like values and the narrowest SameSite policy.

findings.summary: The fresh page has a broad third-party collection and execution footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker probe saw 11 third-party origins including GTM; HAR attributes 112/119 requests and 3.30MB to non-main-origin hosts.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat Zoom-owned subdomains as a first-party boundary where justified, but defer analytics/chat until consent and remove vendors that do not support the task.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers probe found no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or X-Content-Type-Options; HSTS was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors, nosniff, a strict referrer policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; evaluate Trusted Types for script-heavy surfaces.

findings.summary: The contact-sales form disables useful autofill.
findings.evidence: Form probe shows email, name, phone, postal code, company and job-title controls all use autocomplete=off.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic autocomplete tokens such as email, given-name, family-name, tel, postal-code, organization and organization-title.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and misses responsive sizing.
findings.evidence: Image probe found 37 legacy-format images, 20 missing srcset and two oversized images; Lighthouse estimates 317KiB image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP where appropriate, add srcset/sizes and ensure image requests match rendered size.

findings.summary: Initial third-party and media weight is disproportionate to the first task.
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 3.34MB: 1.64MB images, 0.97MB scripts and 0.30MB fonts; chat and GTM load before user intent.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route-level budget, defer chat/carousels and below-fold media, and subset/preload only necessary fonts.

findings.summary: Agent-facing capability is not exposed on the public task surface.
findings.evidence: Page probe found no WebMCP capability while the site promotes AI products and links to Zoom developer MCP material.
findings.suggestedFix: For safe high-value actions, expose constrained WebMCP tools or agentic forms with explicit user confirmation.

findings.summary: Repeated disclosure interaction retained materially more heap in the post snapshot.
findings.evidence: After 20 repeated clicks, heap self-size rose 27.17MB to 31.63MB (+16%), node count 393,355 to 470,476 and closures 16,050 to 21,068. Separate-run snapshots make causality medium confidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Reproduce in one controlled session with baseline/target/final snapshots and GC, then remove accumulating listeners, closures or cached state revealed by retaining paths.
